newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see rand issues, await large dollar deal.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see rand issues, await large dollar deal.

text.p: The primary market saw the first South African subsidiary enter the Eurorand sector in a relatively subdued session on Tuesday afternoon.

German chemicals and drugs group subsidiary Bayer Pty Ltd -- which is wholly owned and has a support agreement from its parent Bayer AG -- launched the deal via lead manager Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
The paper pays a 15.375 percent coupon.
"There is ongoing demand for Eurorand paper," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell syndicate manager Roger Bates said.

"There are investors who are taking the view South African interest rates will decline in the medium-term, so with a four-year issue such as today, there is the possibility of capital appreciation," Bates said.
"Investors will therefore want to be sure of their credit, and Bayer certainly fits the bill."
Bayer AG is rated Aa2 by Moody's Investors Service and AA by Standard & Poor's Corp.
Meanwhile the World Bank increased its two-year 15.0 percent bond by 100 million rand to 400 million rand via Hambros Bank.
Hambros Bank syndicate manager said the deal was increased due to the strong demand.
"Key areas of demand are Italy, Switzerland, Benelux, Germany and to a lesser extent funds in Britain and the Middle East...it has a well-spread distribution," he said.
"There is fresh money flowing into the system especially in the light of the strength of the currency and the underlying bond market."
Meanwhile a number of large dollar deals are expected soon. General Motors Acceptance Corp will launch a $1.0 billion five-year global bond later this week, J.P. Morgan said.

Merrill Lynch will also be joint lead manager. GMAC, rated A3/A-, last issued an international dollar bond last November with a $200 million four-year deal at a spread of 32 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
Also, Osaka Gas Co Ltd will launch a dollar-denominated Eurobond for around $400 million this week, lead manager Goldman Sachs said. The maturity is expected at 10 years.
Market sources said a spread of around 40 basis points over U.S. Treasuries was likely.
Osaka is rated Aa2 by Moody's Investors Service and AA- by Standard & Poor's Corp.
In the emerging market sector, Russia's United Export Import Bank (Uneximbank) plans to launch a debut public Eurobond for up to $200 million, its head of treasury, Alexander Popov, said on Tuesday.
"The estimated size is between $100 million and $200 million. It will be a straight bond for between three to five years," he said.
A mandate for the deal would be awarded by the end of this week, he added.
-- Hayley Pienaar, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
